Apex-iCore Handbook

Hot castings give their heat to air. The air preheats the scrap, and the scrap goes straight into the induction furnace. The hourly pit cycle is the Heat Boomerang.

01 · The design

How the machine physically works

Hot castings preheat the next charge of scrap. Air carries the heat, the scrap stores it, and the furnace uses it. No fuel, no steam, no pressure.

1Shakeout500°C castings, 30 sets of 33.3 kg an hour
→
2Jib + airlockset hung on a hook, pedal opens the outer door
→
3Tunnel 20 m140 min; air 35 → 398°C, counterflow
→
4Settling boxsand drops out of the air
→
53 pits + spareair flows down through 1 t baskets
→
6Hopperhot basket ≈ 326°C into the furnace
Castings in → out500 → 120°C
Air in → out of tunnel35 → 398°C
Air through the pits396 → 80°C
Hot basket to furnace≈ 326°C
Exhaust36–84°C

Air through the three pits in series: 396 → 253 → 125 → 80°C.

Subsystems

SubsystemKey figures
Recovery tunnel20 m, 0.9 × 0.9 m inside, 300 mm rock wool
Fins, hot 10 m100 × 2 mm plates every 50 mm, ≈ 3× the wall area
Stirring fans5 fans, 2 m/s, tilted 12° toward the hot end so the air corkscrews along the tunnel
Hook loop≈ 77 trolleys on a rail inside the tunnel; one push every 2 min moves the line 0.286 m
Airlocks2 doors each, never open together; tunnel held at −8 Pa
Settling box9 m/s duct opens into a 0.3 m/s box, so sand falls out
Scrap pits4 pits, 1.6 × 1.6 × 2.6 m, sand-trough seals; 3 in series, 1 spare
Dampers12 manual (H, L, X); 6 levers each hour
ExhaustBag filter, 0.75 kW fan with VFD, whole line under suction

Operating cycle: two rhythms

Every 2 minThe tunnel
0:00Inner doors open; the line moves one hook
0:15Pusher returns; inner doors close
0:30Exit door opens; a set rolls out at 120°C
0:40Unloader bins the castings, returns the hook
1:00Jib hangs the next 500°C set on a hook
1:40Pedal: outer door opens, trolley enters
Minute of the hourThe pits
0–16 damper levers: air to the next basket
1–3Crane lifts the hood off the hottest pit
3–5Hot basket, ≈ 326°C, to the hopper
5–6Lid opens, bottom drops, scrap falls in
6–9Empty basket to the yard; hood back on
9–55Charger feeds hot scrap to the furnace
11–25Yard refills the empty basket
30–36Refilled basket into the spare pit

Pit rotation: the air moves, not the baskets. Each hour every role (hottest, middle, coolest, spare) shifts one pit along. That takes 6 levers and 1 minute, instead of 3 hot basket lifts. From a cold start the scrap warms from 28 to 42 kWh/t over a 16-hour day; the year average is 41.1 kWh/t into the scrap.

The physics behind 52 kWh per tonne

Counterflow, matched
  • Castings 0.17 kW/K against air 0.15 kW/K.
  • So the air leaves within about 100 K of 500°C.
Why downflow
  • Bed friction 0.1–0.2 Pa against hot-air buoyancy 0.3–2 Pa.
  • Gravity steers the air, so it must flow down through the scrap.
Settling (Stokes)
  • 100 µm sand falls at 0.44 m/s.
  • The box air moves at 0.3 m/s, so the sand drops out.
Fans and pressure
  • ≈ 1,000 Pa budget, 700 of it the filter.
  • Exhaust fan ≈ 0.29 kW; all running power 6,294 kWh a year.

Safety: every failure cools it down and lets air in

HazardDetected byPrevention and response
Wet scrapYard check, weightPreheat dries it before the melt; baskets drain
Oily scrapCO/VOC sensor, filter ΔpSegregate at the yard; air capped at ≈ 400°C
Over-heatThermocouplesAlarms at 420°C in the tunnel, 110°C at the filter
Fan stopsManometer, motor currentPedal locked; doors stay shut; castings cool
Stuck damperPit in/out temperaturePanel lamps show the pattern; freed by hand
Pit fireOutlet hotter than inletClose its H damper to starve it of air
Door crushDoor position switchesInterlocks, guard rails, E-stop
Power cut—Nothing pressurised; doors spring shut
PLC decides
  • Airlock sequence, pusher, suction loop, alarms and logging.
AI advises
  • Change-over timing, anomaly warnings, savings reports.
  • Never overrides an interlock.
Human override
  • Manual dampers, pusher hand valve, key-switch doors, E-stop.
  • Runs with the PLC off.

Interlocks: one airlock's two doors never open together · the pedal is ignored without suction · the pusher runs only with the inner door fully open.

03 · Materials, fan speed and time in the tunnel

One tunnel, twelve alloys: set the fan, keep the strength

Locked design: 20 m tunnel, 0.9 × 0.9 m, 1 t/h, 33 kg sets, 28 mm equivalent section.

Fan speed and time inside the tunnel

Main fan rated 0.25 kg/s (≈ 785 m³/h) at 50 Hz; flow is set on the VFD. The conveyor is the same for every material: 0.143 m/min, one 33 kg set every 2 min, 0.29 m hook pitch, 140 min inside. Airflow matches each material's heat-capacity rate (about 1.05×).

Air speed in the tunnel: 0.17 m/s (cold end) to 0.38 m/s (hot end) for irons; 0.26 to 0.55 m/s for aluminium. Aluminium needs more air and 4 m/s stirring because its emissivity is low (~0.2).

Gentler than the floor
  • The tunnel takes 133–137 min to reach 120°C vs 75–98 min on the floor (about 1.6–1.8× slower), so cracking risk drops.
Thin-vs-thick difference
  • 131°C in the tunnel vs 250°C on the floor for irons; stress falls from 0.5–0.6 to 0.25–0.3 of UTS.
Tightest cases
  • Stainless, aluminium and gunmetal reach about 0.5–0.6 of UTS in the tunnel (0.8–1.0 on the floor), so keep section changes gradual.
Hooks
  • Aluminium at 400°C is very weak: use mesh trays, no piercing hooks, no heavy hanging loads.
Leaded alloys
  • Lead is liquid above 327°C; avoid shock or heavy hook load until below that.

Thick castings (75 mm equivalent): half-throughput mode

At normal settings a 75 mm section exits at 195–214°C and recovery falls to ~33 kWh/t. For thick castings run half throughput with half the airflow.

MaterialFan (kg/s)Hook intervalTime insideReaches 150°CExits
Irons0.077–0.0814 min280 min243–245 min123–126°C
Steels0.0814 min280 min253 min132°C
Stainless / duplex0.0764 min280 min266–269 min142–144°C
Aluminium0.118–0.1194 min280 min245 min117–119°C
Copper alloys0.056–0.0654 min280 min236–246 min121–128°C

Thin sections (10 mm) exit at 59–73°C and recover about 45–48 kWh/t. Below about 20 Hz use a damper or bypass instead of running the motor slower.

Panel settings and limits

On the panel
  • Recipe: alloy, fan Hz, stirring m/s, hook interval. Exit IR pyrometer confirms ≤ 150°C.
Operating rules
  • Maximum entry temperature about 550°C.
  • One alloy family at a time, with separate scrap baskets.

Limits: model predictions, not measurements. Metallurgical time limits are handbook order-of-magnitude values, not a kinetic simulation. Stresses use room-temperature modulus and UTS (conservative, especially for aluminium and copper). Actual section thickness decides which mode to use.

04 · Pilot, team and vision

From model to measured savings in 15 months

Maturity today: system TRL 3, parts TRL 8–9. Designed, modelled and simulated; not yet tested with real castings and scrap.

  1. Months 0–3 · Bench test2.5 m tunnel section with real castings: radiation, fins, fans.
  2. Months 2–4 · Single hot pitReal scrap and a 400°C heater: downflow, bed pressure drop, sand seals.
  3. Months 3–6 · Pilot designPartner foundry, layout, ADEETIE energy audit and detailed project report.
  4. Months 6–12 · Pilot buildFull Apex-iCore at 1 t/h in a Coimbatore foundry.
  5. Months 12–15 · MeasurePaired heats on the furnace meter, verified by an auditor.
Success criterionTargetModel
Furnace electricity saved≥ 45 kWh/t52.5
Heat delivered in scrap≥ 35 kWh/t39.35
Casting exit temperature≤ 150°C≈ 120
Tunnel suctionbelow −3 Pa always−8 Pa
Uptime, production hours≥ 95%—
Payback on measured data≤ 3 years2.4

The narrated 3D tour walks through a 1 t/h foundry in 15 chapters, about 12 minutes: furnace, pouring and shakeout, the jib, pedal and airlocks, a thermal camera inside the tunnel, the fins and tilted fans, the settling-box swirl, every pit part, the hourly crane change-over and a live energy meter. Every colour and temperature comes from the physics model.

Why Apex-iCore should continue

Market
  • ≈ 5,000 Indian foundries, 90% MSMEs, 15.9 Mt a year; clusters from Coimbatore to Rajkot.
Next uses
  • Forgings heating billets, heat-treat loads, die-casting, ceramic kilns.
Product path
  • Manual build → motorised, PLC-controlled version → digital-twin service.
  • Licensed to cluster fabricators, ESCO or ADEETIE-financed.

Castings leave the mould at 500°C. Apex-iCore sends that heat back: 52 kWh/t, ₹20 lakh a year, about a 2.4-year payback, built locally.
